# SetAnimKey <img class="product" src="media/b3d-20x14.png" alt="Blitz3D" title="Blitz3D" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Animation](Blitz3D-Animation)

</div>


```blitzbasic
SetAnimKey:Void entity:Int32, frame:Int32, pos_key:Int32=1, rot_key:Int32=1, scale_key:Int32=1
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | In | Int32 | required | The entity whose pose is recorded. |
| `frame` | In | Int32 | required | Frame number of the key, starting at 0. |
| `pos_key` | In | Int32 | `1` | True to store the position. Defaults to True. |
| `rot_key` | In | Int32 | `1` | True to store the rotation. Defaults to True. |
| `scale_key` | In | Int32 | `1` | True to store the scale. Defaults to True. |

## Description

Records the entity's current position, rotation and scale as a keyframe at the given frame. After the keys are made, [AddAnimSeq](AddAnimSeq) turns them into a sequence that [Animate](Animate) and [SetAnimTime](SetAnimTime) can play, with the frames between the keys interpolated. Use it on the bones of a hand-built model or on any entity that you want to animate by keys.

Each of the three flags decides which part of the pose is stored. Setting a key again at the same frame replaces the old one.
